title: Connecticut (Carman's River)
summary: Connecticut names a Brookhaven creek or river now known as Carman's River. The name appears in early Mastic-area boundary language and should not be confused with the New England river or the modern state.
address_label: Carman's River, Brookhaven, NY (approximate general location)
map_geometry_source: Connecticut is identified as a Brookhaven creek or river now called Carman's River. Point is an approximate/general marker along Carman's River, not an exact historic coordinate.
why_this_matters: Connecticut, as an early name for Carman's River, preserves a Native descriptor meaning at the long river or long tidal creek. The name shows that familiar Algonquian place-language could appear in multiple regions while still describing a specific Long Island waterway. Carman's River belongs to Indigenous geography as a named, remembered river, not only as a later colonial or modern landmark.
history_content: This placename belongs to meadow and boundary descriptions near Mastic. East Connecticut distinguished this river from West Connecticut, the Islip stream now called Connetquot.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Connecticut and Conitticut. The name is interpreted as a common Algonquian term for a long tidal river or creek, meaning at the long river.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names reflect cultural views and power dynamics.”

— New Zealand Ministry of Education, New Zealand Curriculum: Social Sciences, Years 9–10 (2025), ‘Cultural meaning and place names’ section

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
land_loss_content: A name now associated mainly with New England also belonged to Long Island river geography. The deed references preserve Native place-language within colonial descriptions of meadow, river, and Mastic lands.
whereintheworld_content: Carman's River in Brookhaven is the general waterway associated with this placename. The sources do not establish a surveyed historic boundary.
